description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:160 — \`pub const fn new(logs: CtLogList, verifier: V) -> Self\`
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:166 — \`pub const fn logs(&self) -> &CtLogList\`

Once \`const fn\` ships in a public API surface, removing \`const\` is a breaking change for any caller invoking it in a \`const\` context (\`const FOO: SctVerifier<_> = SctVerifier::new(...);\`, \`static\` initialiser, or other \`const fn\` body).

Neither function appears to NEED \`const\`-ness:

- \`new\` takes a \`CtLogList\` (which contains a \`BTreeMap<[u8;32], CtLog>\`) and a \`V: SignatureVerifier\`. Neither can be constructed in \`const\` context in practice (BTreeMap::new is const, but populating it via \`insert\` is not), so the const-ness of \`new\` is theoretical.
- \`logs\` returns \`&CtLogList\` — also unreachable in \`const\` for the same reason.

If the maintainer later wants to change the internal layout (e.g. lazily compute a SHA-256 cache, take a \`RwLock\` for hot-reload of the log list), \`const fn\` blocks that refactor unless they bump major.

Suggested fix: drop \`const\` from both unless there's a concrete consumer demonstrably calling them in const context. Pre-1.0 the cost of dropping is zero; post-1.0 it's a major-version cost.

Priority: P4 — there's no functional bug; this is forward-compat hardening. Possibly \`opinion\` if you disagree the const-ness is gratuitous.
title: (api-contract) SctVerifier::new and ::logs marked pub const fn — locks in const-callability across MSRV
